findings.name: Unauthenticated OS command injection in new /ping endpoint (shell=True)
findings.description: Any unauthenticated caller can run arbitrary OS commands as the app user and read the output in the HTTP response — e.g. `GET /ping?host=127.0.0.1;cat%20/etc/passwd`. The new endpoint concatenates the `host` query parameter straight into a shell string passed to `subprocess.check_output(..., shell=True)` with no validation, allowlist or quoting, and the route is registered on the shared Flask app which has no auth middleware.
findings.attackScript: host = request.args.get("host", "") (ping.py:10) → subprocess.check_output("ping -c 1 " + host, shell=True) (ping.py:11); output returned to caller.

findings.name: SQL injection in new /search route: raw `q` param concatenated into LIKE clause
findings.description: An unauthenticated request to `/search` can read any table in the SQLite database — e.g. `/search?q=%25' UNION SELECT sql FROM sqlite_master--` returns the injected rows verbatim in the JSON response. The `q` query parameter is concatenated into a single-quoted LIKE literal with no sanitization, so a quote in `q` terminates the literal and appends arbitrary SQL. The sibling `/user` route uses a bound parameter, so this is a local deviation, not a codebase-wide pattern. `limit` is separately clamped by `page_size()` and is not the issue.
findings.attackScript: q = request.args.get("q", "") (line 34) → cur.execute("SELECT name FROM users WHERE name LIKE '%" + q + "%' LIMIT " + str(limit)) (line 37) → return {"rows": cur.fetchall()} (line 38)
